articles.title: Elected Somali daycare owner with fraud ties now revealed to also be married to illegal immigrant
articles.summary: Fox News Digital confirmed Minnesota DFL Rep. Abdi Daisane's wife, Ayaan Aydid, is in the U.S. illegally after crossing the southern border in 2023.
articles.body:
A Somali politician whose daycare business has been tied to fraud is married to an illegal alien, Fox News Digital has confirmed.

Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party (DFL) candidate Abdi Daisane defeated a Republican incumbent to win Minnesota's House District 14A seat, which encompasses some of the city of St. Cloud.

Daisane's wife, Ayaan Aydid, 30, is present in the country illegally, a Trump administration official confirmed on Wednesday afternoon after an Alpha News report on the subject. Aydid crossed the U.S. southern border with Mexico in 2023, during former President Joe Biden's administration.

After Daisane's victory, a video surfaced of Aydid detailing to the BBC how she crossed into the United States at the southern border, sparking questions about her immigration status . An accompanying story describes Aydid as "one of hundreds of Somalis who have jumped the US-Mexico border wall."

"It wasn't a hard journey," she said in the interview.

Daisane, who delivered part of his victory speech in Somali, is the CEO of Blooming Kids Child Care Center in St. Cloud, which has received $7.29 million from the state-run Child Care Assistance Program since 2018.

His childcare business also received $598,251.62 from the federally-funded Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) since 2020. A nonprofit called Partners in Nutrition, which recently had to pay an $18.5 million civil settlement for fraud, was the center's sponsor for CACFP funds.

A press release from the settlement says Partners in Nutrition "knowingly defrauded the State of Minnesota out of millions of dollars in federal child nutrition funds during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, in violation of the Minnesota False Claims Act."

Fox News Digital visited Daisane's business in St. Cloud just after his election and found a quiet scene.

A paper sign on a wooden front door that faces the street directs visitors to a different entrance. The floor-to-ceiling glass windows next to the door are covered with a tinted and mirrored film.

The building is flanked by a parking lot that was mostly empty.

Behind the building is a tiny fenced-in playground, anchored by two children's jungle gyms. There were no children playing at the time.

Daisane didn't return Fox News Digital's comment request.

"Our nation's immigration laws apply to EVERYONE, and the men and women of ICE will enforce them, regardless of political status or power," Immigration and Customs Enforcement posted on X.

images.caption: A small outdoor play area at the Blooming Kids Child Care Center in St. Cloud, Minn., on Nov. 5, 2026. The center is owned by state Rep.-elect Abdi Daisane.

articles.title: Paciente usa bolsa para apoiar braço em cadeira com defeito em P.U | G1
articles.standfirst: Secretaria Municipal de Saúde afirma que mobiliário tem mais de 10 anos de uso e será substituído.
articles.summary: Secretaria Municipal de Saúde afirma que mobiliário tem mais de 10 anos de uso e será substituído.
articles.body:
Uma paciente usou a própria bolsa para apoiar o braço durante o atendimento no Posto de Urgência Dr. Munir Bussad, conhecido como PU de Itaperuna , no Noroeste Fluminense. A poltrona em que ela estava sentada estava com o apoio de braço danificado, com parte do revestimento solta.

No vídeo gravado por quem acompanhava a paciente, ela mostra a parte solta do apoio e, em seguida, coloca a bolsa entre o braço e a estrutura da poltrona.

"Tem que colocar a bolsa para firmar o braço. " disse paciente.

Durante atendimento, mulher usou a própria bolsa para apoiar o braço em poltrona com defeito — Foto: Blog do Reverendo

O secretário municipal de Saúde, Sávio Saboia, afirmou que as cadeiras são antigas e estimou que tenham mais de 10 anos de uso. Segundo ele, o município já comprou novas cadeiras para substituir as atuais, com entrega prevista para dezembro.

As imagens também mostram outras poltronas na mesma sala com rasgos nos assentos e encostos, além de partes do estofamento faltando.

articles.title: 'Sempre preocupada com todos', lamenta neta de idosa que morreu na tempestade em Tupanciretã | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa Civil contabilizou 60 feridos e 3 mortes. Município está sem energia elétrica e abastecimento de água.
articles.summary: Defesa Civil contabilizou 60 feridos e 3 mortes. Município está sem energia elétrica e abastecimento de água.
articles.body:
Hortência tinha 85 anos e morreu durante tempestade no RS — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Hortência Bueno Alves, 85 anos, é uma das vítimas da tempestade que atingiu Tupanciretã na madrugada desta sexta-feira (20).

Ela estava em casa, acompanhada da nora, quando a residência veio abaixo.

Hortência não resistiu aos ferimentos e faleceu antes da chegada do socorro. A nora ficou presa nos escombros, mas posteriormente foi socorrida e passa bem.

A neta Ethyane Alves lamentou a morte de Hortência:

"Minha vó era uma pessoa incrível, alto astral, adorava estar com a família e sempre preocupada com todos".

A tempestade que atingiu Tupanciretã, cidade de 20 mil habitantes na Região Central do Rio Grande do Sul, durante a madrugada desta sexta-feira (20) causou 3 mortes e deixou 60 feridos, conforme a Defesa Civil.

No centro da cidade, as ruas ficaram cobertas de granizo e destroços de edificações, árvores e postes de energia elétrica. De acordo com o prefeito, praticamente todas as residências da cidade foram atingidas.

“Destruiu a cidade. Nós temos 8,6 mil casas, e acho que 8 mil estão destruídas, destelhadas ou derrubadas”, disse o prefeito Gustavo Herter Terra.

Até o início da manhã, a prefeitura não havia contabilizado o número de feridos nem tinha dimensão dos prejuízos provocados pelo temporal. A suspeita é que a cidade tenha sido atingida por um tornado , segundo o chefe do Executivo.

Ainda segundo o prefeito, prédios importantes foram atingidos, como o único hospital da cidade. Há também problemas no fornecimento de energia elétrica, distribuição de água e no sinal de telefonia.

"Tivemos óbito, muitos feridos. Estamos transportando nossos feridos para Santa Maria e para Júlio de Castilhos ( cidades vizinhas ). Nosso hospital também foi destelhado, não temos mais raio-x, nem ultrassom. A situação é bem complicada", afirma.

O Corpo de Bombeiros e a Defesa Civil prestam atendimento à população afetada. O governador Eduardo Leite prestou solidariedade à cidade por meio de uma publicação nas redes sociais.

"Já conversei com o prefeito Gustavo Terra logo pela manhã e determinei a mobilização de força total do Governo do Estado para atender a população. Nossas equipes da Defesa Civil, Corpo de Bombeiros, Brigada Militar e demais órgãos estaduais estão sendo mobilizadas.

O Centro de Monitoramento da Defesa Civil do RS analisou imagens e vídeos da tempestade que atingiu Tupanciretã na madrugada desta sexta-feira. Há indícios de que a cidade tenha sido atingida por uma microexplosão . Uma estação do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) registrou rajadas de vento de 114 km/h durante o temporal.

"Até o momento, não é possível confirmar a ocorrência de um tornado no município. As evidências apontam para ventos severos associados à supercélula, possivelmente provocados por uma microexplosão. A possibilidade de tornado não está completamente descartada, mas o fenômeno, isoladamente, não explicaria a extensão dos danos registrados na cidade", destaca a Defesa Civil.

Os dados do radar meteorológico de Porto Alegre indicam a atuação da supercélula por volta das 3h19.

A Defesa Civil do RS emitiu, às 2h38, um alerta vermelho por SMS para a região, incluindo Tupanciretã, indicando risco de granizo grande e vendaval, com risco muito alto de destelhamentos. O alerta teve vigência até as 3h37.

articles.title: Vagas de emprego: Shoppings de Piracicaba e Limeira abrem 1 mil postos | G1
articles.standfirst: Oportunidades incluem contratos temporários de 45 dias e vagas efetivas para atender à demanda da Black Friday, do Natal e das liquidações de início de ano; seleções aceitam candidatos sem experiência.
articles.summary: Vagas de emprego em Piracicaba e Limeira oferecem postos em lojas e restaurantes para o fim de ano, com seleções abertas inclusive para candidatos sem experiência.
articles.body:
A aproximação da Black Friday e das festas de fim e virada de ano, com Natal e réveillon, impulsionam contratações no setor varejista da região, que oferecem vagas temporárias e efetivas. Os shoppings Piracicaba (SP) e Limeira (SP) disponibilizam mais de mil postos de trabalho para lojas, restaurantes e prestadores de serviços.

Há vagas para atendentes, estoquista, caixa, garçon, operador comercial e mais. Os salários são acima do piso de mercado, com variação entre R$ 2 mil e R$ 5 mil, além de benefícios. As remunerações são específicas para cada estabelecimento.Veja detalhes sobre as oportunidades e como se candidatar, abaixo, na reportagem.

No Shopping Piracicaba, a expectativa é gerar quase mil oportunidades para reforçar o atendimento durante a Black Friday, no fim de novembro, o Natal e as liquidações de janeiro.

Entre os destaques estão os contratos temporários com duração de 45 dias. Além disso, de 10% a 15% do total de vagas são efetivas, destinadas a novos empreendimentos que estão se instalando no local.

De acordo com o superintendente do Shopping Piracicaba, Rodrigo Matouk, o período representa o momento de maior intensidade para o comércio.

"A estimativa habitual é de um aumento de 5% a 6% no fluxo de visitantes em novembro", detalhou. O índice que deve ser ainda maior neste ano devido aos feriados, chegando a um crescimento de 20% a 30% no fluxo e nas vendas em dezembro.

Movimento de consumidores em shopping de Piracicaba — Foto: Claudia Assencio/g1/ Arquivo

Para suprir essa demanda, a maioria dos lojistas deve contratar de três a quatro funcionários adicionais.

As oportunidades são abertas inclusive para quem não possui experiência prévia, sendo a disponibilidade de dias e horários um fator decisivo na seleção. Segundo Rodrigo Matouk, a forma de candidatura varia conforme o perfil do estabelecimento:

Lojas de franqueados ou proprietários locais: os interessados devem comparecer pessoalmente ao estabelecimento e procurar a gerência, que fará o encaminhamento para a seleção.

Lojas de grandes marcas e redes: os candidatos devem acessar o site oficial das respectivas empresas e buscar o link para as plataformas de recrutamento online.

Disponibilidade e bom atendimento são diferenciais

Para quem deseja aproveitar as oportunidades, algumas características podem fazer a diferença nos processos seletivos, segundo o Shopping Piracicaba.

Entre elas estão a disponibilidade para trabalhar em diferentes dias e horários, incluindo finais de semana e feriados, a facilidade de relacionamento com o público, a disposição para aprender e o interesse em desenvolver habilidades profissionais.

O ambiente de shopping exige dinamismo e capacidade de adaptação, mas também oferece experiências em diferentes segmentos do varejo e possibilidades de crescimento.

Pátio Limeira Shopping — Foto: Pátio Limeira Shopping/Divulgação

Em Limeira, o Pátio Limeira Shopping também ampliou o quadro de contratações, oferecendo mais de 60 vagas fixas e temporárias. As funções disponíveis incluem cargos como bilheteiro, operador de caixa, vendedor e estoquista, entre outros.

Para conferir detalhes sobre salários, carga horária, benefícios e requisitos, os candidatos devem ir diretamente às lojas e aos restaurantes do centro de compras.

Vitrines também estão com avisos indicando o recrutamento. Ao entrar nos estabelecimentos, o interessado obtém todas as informações e pode iniciar imediatamente a participação no processo seletivo.

articles.title: What are the implications of the ICJ Rohingya genocide ruling?
articles.summary: Verdict against Myanmar may have implications for Israel’s genocide in Gaza.
articles.body:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Muslim Rohingya minority.

Thousands of people were killed in a 2017 crackdown that forced nearly one million Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh.

So, how significant is this ruling? And are there implications for Israel’s genocide in Gaza?

articles.title: Por que o Sul é a região do Brasil mais propícia a supercélulas | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Climatempo, posição geográfica favorece encontros mais intensos entre massas de ar quente e frio. Tempestades podem provocar ventos acima de 90 km/h, granizo e tornados.
articles.summary: Segundo a Climatempo, posição geográfica favorece contrastes de temperatura e umidade. Supercélulas podem provocar ventos acima de 90 km/h, granizo e tornados.
articles.body:
A tempestade que atingiu Tupanciretã, no Rio Grande do Sul, nesta sexta-feira (20), voltou a chamar atenção para um tipo de fenômeno capaz de provocar ventos muito fortes, granizo e chuva intensa em pouco tempo: as supercélulas .

Segundo a Climatempo, o Sul é a região do Brasil mais propícia à formação dessas tempestades . A explicação está principalmente na posição geográfica dos três estados e na frequência com que diferentes massas de ar se encontram sobre a região.

É no Sul que o ar frio de origem polar costuma chegar primeiro e com maior intensidade. Ao mesmo tempo, correntes de vento transportam ar quente e úmido de áreas mais ao norte do continente.

Quando esse contraste ocorre em um ambiente com muita umidade e condições favoráveis à formação de grandes nuvens, a atmosfera pode ficar especialmente instável.

📝 ENTENDA: As supercélulas são grandes nuvens de tempestade que se desenvolvem tanto horizontalmente quanto verticalmente. Elas podem provocar rajadas acima de 90 km/h , grandes volumes de chuva em pouco tempo, granizo, microexplosões e até tornados.

No caso de Tupanciretã, a Defesa Civil do Rio Grande do Sul apontou preliminarmente para ventos severos associados a uma supercélula, possivelmente causados por uma microexplosão . A ocorrência de tornado não foi totalmente descartada.

Uma estação do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia ( Inmet ) registrou rajada de 114,8 km/h na cidade durante a madrugada.

De acordo com o Centro de Monitoramento da Defesa Civil, uma supercélula avançou sobre a região de Tupanciretã. — Foto: Reprodução/RBS TV

A formação dessas tempestades depende da combinação de diferentes condições na atmosfera.

Entre elas estão baixa pressão, grande disponibilidade de umidade, forte contraste de temperatura e mudanças importantes na velocidade e na direção do vento conforme a altitude.

Esse último fator é chamado de cisalhamento do vento e ajuda a organizar e favorecer o giro das nuvens.

A passagem de frentes frias e de outros sistemas atmosféricos também pode contribuir para o desenvolvimento vertical das tempestades.

Supercélulas podem surgir em outras regiões do Brasil e em qualquer época do ano. Primavera e verão, porém, costumam oferecer condições mais favoráveis porque a atmosfera está mais quente e úmida.

Os meteorologistas conseguem prever com antecedência de até cerca de 48 horas quando o ambiente estará favorável à formação dessas tempestades.

A confirmação de uma supercélula específica, porém, depende do acompanhamento por radares meteorológicos e imagens de satélite.

Supercélula é registrada por caçadores de tempestades na região de Alegrete, no Rio Grande do Sul, durante temporal em setembro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube

O El Niño em curso também entra nessa equação, mas não significa que o fenômeno cause diretamente tornados, microexplosões ou tempestades severas.

Segundo a Climatempo, o El Niño pode tornar mais frequente a combinação de fatores que favorece episódios de tempo severo no Sul.

Uma das mudanças ocorre no chamado Jato de Baixos Níveis , uma corrente de ventos que transporta ar quente e úmido da Amazônia para outras regiões da América do Sul.

Durante episódios de El Niño, essa corrente tende a ficar mais frequentemente direcionada e intensa sobre o Paraguai, o norte da Argentina e o Sul do Brasil, aumentando a oferta de calor e umidade necessária para a formação de grandes áreas de tempestade.

Ao mesmo tempo, frentes frias continuam avançando pelo continente e podem encontrar esse ar quente e úmido. É justamente a repetição desses encontros que aumenta o risco de episódios severos.

Uma incrível supercélula (tipo de tempestade) se forma sobre a cidade de Blackhawk, na Dakota do Sul (EUA), na imagem de James Smart — Foto: James Smart

No sábado (21), o Sul ainda terá períodos de sol e calor, com temperaturas de 30°C ou mais em várias áreas.

Mesmo assim, a combinação de calor, umidade e uma área de baixa pressão deve favorecer novas pancadas de chuva , principalmente à tarde e à noite.

No Rio Grande do Sul, os temporais isolados são mais prováveis no Norte e no Noroeste , com possibilidade de granizo e rajadas acima de 80 km/h. Santa Catarina pode ter chuva mais forte no Norte e no Vale do Itajaí, enquanto, no Paraná, os maiores volumes devem atingir o Sul, o Oeste e o Noroeste.

No domingo (22), o risco aumenta novamente. Um ciclone extratropical próximo ao Rio Grande do Sul, associado a uma nova frente fria, deve reforçar as instabilidades nos três estados.

A previsão indica possibilidade de temporais com granizo e rajadas acima de 80 km/h no Rio Grande do Sul, principalmente no Noroeste, Norte, Nordeste, Serra, Litoral Norte e Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre.

Em Santa Catarina, a chuva aumenta nas áreas centrais e serranas, e, no Paraná, os temporais devem se concentrar principalmente no Oeste e no Sul.

articles.title: Tempestade deixa estragos em Foz do Iguaçu e região; veja imagens | G1
articles.standfirst: Paraná está sob alerta amarelo do Inmet, que indica a possibilidade de ventos de até 60 km/h, queda de granizo e chuvas fortes.
articles.summary: Paraná está sob alerta amarelo do Inmet, que indica a possibilidade de ventos de até 60 km/h, queda de granizo e chuvas fortes.
articles.body:
Uma tempestade deixou estragos em Foz do Iguaçu , no oeste do Paraná, na tarde desta sexta-feira (20). Outras cidades da região também foram afetadas.

O Paraná está sob alerta amarelo do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet), que indica a possibilidade de ventos de até 60 km/h, queda de granizo e chuvas fortes. Uma área de baixa pressão sobre o norte da Argentina e o Paraguai ganha força e favorece maior transporte de umidade. Com isso, no sudoeste do estado, a chuva aumenta, especialmente próximo à divisa com Santa Catarina e à fronteira com a Argentina.

Após a tempestade, municípios do Oeste e do Sudoeste do Paraná registraram interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica. Por volta das 17h, 38.793 unidades consumidoras estavam sem luz em Foz do Iguaçu, segundo a Copel. Em todo o estado, o número de imóveis afetados chegava a 204.528.

Tempestade em Foz do Iguaçu — Foto: Emilson Fernandes

Nuvem em funil, queda de árvores e de postes

Moradores da cidade filmaram, da região central, o momento em que duas nuvens em formato de funil se formaram.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, foram registradas dezenas de quedas de árvores e galhos em vários pontos do município. Situações mais graves foram registradas na área central, Vila Yolanda, Panorama, Bourbom e imediações.

O órgão informou ainda que foram registrados danos em coberturas de várias residências e outros imóveis, principalmente na Região da Vila Iolanda e Centro.

Na Avenida JK, uma das principais da cidade, a força do vento arrancou uma árvore pela raiz. Tronco e galhos obstruíram a via, que precisou ser interditada. Na Avenida Paraná, um salão de beleza e um restaurante ficaram danificados após a queda de um poste e de uma árvore.

Três situações de árvores caídas sobre veículos estacionados foram registradas.

Equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros, da Copel e da Secretaria de Meio Ambiente trabalham no corte e remoção de árvores caídas nas vias públicas, sobre a rede elétrica e sobre residências.

Conforme a Defesa Civil, não há registro de feridos e desabrigados.

Veja imagens dos estragos em Foz do Iguaçu:

Tempestade deixa estragos em Foz do Iguaçu — Foto: Kiko Sierich

Outras cidades da região também registraram estragos.

Em Cascavel , por conta da tempestade com raios, o acionamento do número de emergência 193 não está funcionando. O Corpo de Bombeiros pede que, em casos de emergência, a população entre em contato por meio dos telefones (45) 99134-1190, (45) 99134-8482 ou (45) 3220-0005.

No Autódromo Internacional Zilmar Beux, pouco antes do previsto para a prova de automobilismo 40ª Cascavel de Ouro, uma estrutura cedeu. Conforme a organização, uma pessoa teve ferimentos leves e foi atendida. Segundo o diretor do evento, Bento Tino, a chuva destruiu a sala da direção de provas. O equipamento de cronometragem ficou prejudicado e, por isso, a prova foi interrompida e deve ser retomada neste sábado (21).

Ainda na cidade, a chuva, acompanhada de ventos fortes, provocou a destruição de estufas de hidroponia. As estruturas ficaram bastante danificadas. Apesar do prejuízo material, ninguém ficou ferido, já que não havia trabalhadores no local por causa do feriado.

Marmeleiro registrou chuva intensa, acompanhada de fortes rajadas de vento, ocasionando a queda de árvores em diferentes pontos da cidade, além do desprendimento de uma placa de identificação de um estabelecimento comercial.

Segundo a Defesa Civil do município, foram identificadas aproximadamente cinco ocorrências envolvendo árvores. Não houve registro de interrupção no fornecimento de energia elétrica ou nos serviços de internet. A Defesa Civil não registrou solicitações de atendimento relacionadas a destelhamentos ou danos em residências.

Queda de árvore em Marmeleiro — Foto: Defesa Civil

Em Francisco Beltrão , equipes da prefeitura e da Defesa Civil estão mobilizadas para atender às ocorrências relacionadas às chuvas. O município registrou quedas de árvores em alguns pontos da cidade. Em um dos casos, uma rua precisou ser interditada.

Também foram registrados pontos de falta de energia elétrica em diferentes regiões do município, incluindo Seminário, Floresta, Sadia e parte da região central.

articles.title: Rapper Kyivstoner: Rússia teria tentado matar artista na Dinamarca | G1
articles.standfirst: Imprensa local afirma que dois cidadãos dinamarqueses teriam sido contratados para matar o rapper Kyivstoner, que estava no país nórdico para um show.
articles.summary: O Serviço Secreto da Dinamarca impediu o assassinato do rapper Kyivstoner, alvo de um plano russo que envolveu a contratação de dois cidadãos locais em setembro.
articles.body:
O Serviço Secreto da Dinamarca impediu a tentativa de assassinato de um cidadão americano-ucraniano no país. O atentado teria ocorrido em setembro, segundo as autoridades dinamarquesas.

De acordo com informações da DR , emissora pública de rádio da Dinamarca, dois cidadãos dinamarqueses teriam sido contratados para matar o rapper Kyivstoner, considerado pelo governo russo um espião ucraniano. O artista também tem cidadania americana e estava na Dinamarca para um show.

O rapper também já havia sido alvo de um atentado em agosto, durante uma visita à Polônia.

Governo dinamarquês avalia suspender vistos

Após o caso, o governo dinamarquês anunciou nesta sexta-feira (20) que está considerando suspender a concessão de vistos para a zona de livre circulação na Europa, a "Zona Schengen", a cidadãos russos.

"Iniciamos trabalhos em nível europeu para endurecer ainda mais as regras de acesso de cidadãos russos à Europa", disse o Ministro das Relações Exteriores, Lars Lokke Rasmussen. "Estamos agora intensificando nossos esforços, visando à suspensão de todos os vistos não essenciais."

O rapper ucraniano-americano Kyivstoner, que teria sido vítima de um atentado encomendado pelo governo russo. — Foto: Reprodução / Redes Sociais

articles.title: Gil e Margareth participam de caminhada do Ilê Aiyê em Salvador | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor foi homenageado na 23ª edição da celebração que marcou o feriado da Consciência Negra, nesta sexta-feira (20). Cortejo partiu da sede do primeiro bloco afro do Brasil e seguiu pelas ruas do Curuzu e Liberdade.
articles.summary: Cantor foi homenageado na 23ª edição da celebração que marcou o feriado da Consciência Negra, nesta sexta-feira (20)
articles.body:
O cantor Gilberto Gil e a ministra da Cultura Margareth Menezes participaram, nesta sexta-feira (20), da tradicional caminhada promovida pelo bloco afro Ilê Aiyê, em Salvador .

Em sua 23ª edição, o cortejo teve o artista baiano como grande homenageado, com o tema "Andar com Fé pela Paz Mundial".

Na Senzala do Barro Preto, sede do bloco afro, que é o primeiro do Brasil, Gil foi prestigiado pelo afoxé dos Filhos de Gandhy e também recebeu o carinho do povo.

Em seguida, a "Caminhada da Liberdade" partiu pelas ruas dos bairros do Curuzu e Liberdade. Além de Gilberto Gil e Margareth Menezes, a esposa do cantor, Flora Gil, também estava presente. Eles acompanharam o percurso na carroceria de uma caminhonete.

Gilberto Gil e Margareth Menezes participam de caminhada tradicional promovida pelo Ilê Aiyê — Foto: Redes Sociais

O ato, que marcou o feriado da Consciência Negra na capital baiana, defende igualdade racial, valorização da ancestralidade e combate ao racismo.

articles.title: Judaism: What is it like to be Jewish and living in Ireland?
articles.summary: BBC News NI speaks to Jewish people about what it is like to live in the Republic of Ireland.
articles.body:
Naomi Handler has called Ireland home for two decades.

She's among the estimated 2,000 Jewish people living in the country - but has questioned her place in it over the past three years.

A mezuzah, a parchment scroll with a prayer from the Torah, common in Jewish homes, hangs by her front door. "Should I remove it?" she asks.

She is one of a number of Jews who say their experiences of life in the Republic of Ireland have changed since the war in Gaza began.

The conflict was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,700 people have been killed in Israel's military response in Gaza, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

The Irish government condemned the 7 October attack - but it has been a sharp critic of Israel and is a firm supporter of a Palestinian state, independent of Israel.

Pro-Palestinian sentiment is common in Irish society too.

A campaign to stop the Irish international football team playing Israel; the country's public service broadcaster boycotting Eurovision due to Israel's participation; and a sell-out "Free Palestine" concert by US rapper Macklemore in Dublin are just a few examples.

Handler says there seems to be a "collective blame" of Jewish people.

"Should I stop wearing my Star of David? Should I not stop wearing the Star of David necklace? Thoughts that I never had prior to 7 October.

"Ireland was always safe. Ireland is safe. And I still feel, technically speaking, physically safe. Mentally, I'm not necessarily there."

The Irish government's response to the war in Gaza has strained diplomatic relations with Israel to breaking point and Israel closed its embassy in Dublin nearly two years ago.

Handler, who was born in Poland, says she has discussed leaving Ireland with her husband "many times".

"My husband has an American citizenship. We considered that. We considered moving to Israel.

"I think that the big conversation was: where is safe? And that's the trick question. It doesn't feel safe anywhere."

Ria Czerniak-LeBov is an Irish-Jewish artist and writer who is outspoken in her criticism of Israel's actions in the Middle East. She is a member of Jews for Palestine.

She says her views have led to her being called a traitor by some other Jewish people.

"There's a huge amount of online hate from other Jewish communities.

"You get called a kapo, just like a traitor. It's a barbaric term referencing Jews who turned on other Jews during the Holocaust. You get [called] a traitor, you get called a self-hating Jew.

"We're not a monolith - we're just as diverse as any faith or ethnic group."

Czerniak-LeBov says that, in her view, antisemitism is part of a "wider trend of xenophobia and racism".

"I have definitely faced very ignorant comments because I'm Jewish and because my dad is Israeli. I think it's possibly no worse than being any other ethnic minority."

Like Handler, Orli Degani, the chairperson of the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland, says there was a "huge shift" after 7 October.

She is a German Jew and has lived in Ireland for eight years.

"A lot of it became about people seeing us just through the fact that we were born in Israel," she says.

Degani was selected for the Social Democrats party in Ireland's local elections in 2024 but was dropped.

The party said it was because of her stance on Gaza. She says it's because she said at the time that Jewish people felt unwelcome in Ireland.

She says she received emails that included comments and claims such as "all the Jews don't belong in Ireland, get out of Ireland, you know, genocide supporters, baby killers - all of those things".

Ireland's Chief Rabbi Yoni Wieder says many people in the Jewish community feel "very disappointed" by the political climate in the country.

"They're very disappointed by rising incidents of antisemitism," he says.

"That doesn't change the overall feeling of being proud to be Irish and Jewish - but it's really noticeable."

The rabbi said he hears about incidents which people feel are directed at them simply because they are Jewish.

There have been "two or three" physical incidents against Jewish people, he says, but they "aren't common".

"It's certainly safe, in my opinion, for Jewish people to go out and about in the street with identifying features of their Jewish identity, wearing a capote, wearing a Star of David.

"Nevertheless some people do feel uneasy, uncomfortable doing that.

"I've been walking the streets and I've had people shouting at me 'Free Gaza' or 'Zionists out of Ireland', that type of thing.

"Not because they know that I'm the rabbi - just because they see my kippah."

Táiniste (Irish deputy prime minister) Simon Harris described antisemitism as a "scourge" and said he was "really concerned about its rise in Ireland".

Speaking on BBC NI programme The View , Harris, who is the leader of Fine Gael, said the Irish government was "endeavouring to support the Jewish community" through "a range of measures".

He added that the gardaí (Irish police) would "take a very strong line in ensuring that the rights, protections and safety of Jewish people are always upheld".

articles.title: Owaisi-Azad alliance looks strong on paper, but Akhilesh Yadav has little to fear: 5 reasons why SP may not be worried
articles.summary: When Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad joined hands on November 12, the immediate question was whether the alliance of AIMIM and Azad Samaj Party
articles.body: When Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad joined hands on November 12, the immediate question was whether the alliance of AIMIM and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) would become Akhilesh Yadav's biggest worry ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.After all, the two communities they are seeking to mobilise, Muslims and Dalits, are key to Akhilesh's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak backward classes, Dalits and minorities) formula, which helped the Samajwadi Party (SP) emerge as the single-largest party in UP in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.Owaisi had been reaching out to Akhilesh for an alliance since July, even warning him not to regret rejecting the offer if the BJP returned to power. Interestingly, Owaisi was targeting the SP more than the BJP in his election meetings.I am ready to join hands. I am ready to form an alliance. Today is the time to talk. Don't cry later after the elections are over. We don't want the BJP to come to power again.Four months later, with his attempts to forge an alliance with the SP and BSP chief Mayawati yielding no results, Owaisi joined hands with Azad to form the Samajik Parivartan Morcha.Akhilesh, however, appears unfazed. He claimed the new front would cost the BJP, rather than his party, 2-3% of its votes. He also ruled out expanding the SP's existing alliance.An additional option will now be available to such innocent people who cast their votes after being misled. This will cause the BJP a loss of 2-3 per cent votes. The BJP will be left with nothing.So, is Akhilesh right in playing down the threat? Here are five reasons why the Owaisi-Azad alliance may not be as big a worry as it appears.Akhilesh has worked hard to change the SP's pro-Muslim imageAkhilesh Yadav has made a conscious effort to move away from the image of Muslim appeasement that the Samajwadi Party acquired under his father Mulayam Singh Yadav.While Mulayam openly flaunted Muslim voters and built his party's electoral strength around the Muslim-Yadav combination, Akhilesh has been trying to expand the SP's appeal among Hindu voters without alienating its traditional support base.From visiting temples and attending Durga Puja celebrations to hosting iftar gatherings, Akhilesh has been trying to strike a balance between the two communities.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(message,function(e){if(e.data[datawrapper-height]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(iframe);for(var n in e.data[datawrapper-height])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[datawrapper-height][n]+px;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The change became particularly evident after the BJP's sweeping victory in the 2017 assembly elections, when the SP began making Akhilesh's religious engagements more public.Since then, Akhilesh has visited the Vindhyachal temple in Mirzapur and the Ravidas temple in Varanasi, installed a 51-foot statue of Lord Krishna in Saifai and initiated the construction of the Kedareshwar temple in Etawah.On December 12, Akhilesh and his wife Dimple Yadav are scheduled to make their first visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya since its consecration in January 2024.At the same time, his outreach to Muslims has continued. However, Akhilesh has been careful to avoid giving the BJP an opportunity to accuse the SP of Muslim appeasement.Joining hands with Owaisi could undo some of that work and give the BJP fresh ammunition against the SP. By rejecting an alliance with AIMIM, Akhilesh may actually be helping himself retain the broader support base he has built over the years.Azad's primary battle is with MayawatiChandrashekhar Azad is a leader known for taking aggressive political positions that keeps him in the news. But in Uttar Pradesh, he faces a tough challenge from Mayawati, who continues to command the support of a significant section of Dalit voters.Azad's victory from Nagina in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections established him as a Dalit leader to watch. He defeated the BJP candidate by over 1.5 lakh votes, while the SP finished a distant third and the BSP fourth.However, one Lok Sabha victory does not establish Azad as a leader of Dalits across UP. In the 2022 assembly elections, he contested against Yogi Adityanath from Gorakhpur Urban, secured fewer than 8,000 votes and lost his deposit."Jatavs, who account for around 11% of Uttar Pradesh's population, are still largely loyal to Mayawati. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, non-Jatav Dalits, particularly the Pasis, shifted towards the INDIA bloc. This played an important role in the alliance's performance," said Pravin Kumar, senior political observer and Resident Editor of TOI, Lucknow.According to the CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey, 44% of Jatav voters in UP backed the BSP in 2024, even though the party failed to win a single Lok Sabha seat.Moreover, Mayawati has brought her nephew Akash Anand back into the party and reinstated him as national convener, tasking him with expanding the BSP's appeal among young voters.Interestingly, when Mayawati removed Anand from the party in September, Azad had invited him to join the Azad Samaj Party.While Azad enjoys popularity among sections of Dalit youth, his ability to turn that popularity into votes across the state is yet to be established.Owaisi's success in Bihar is no guarantee of success in UPAIMIM won five assembly seats each in Bihar in 2020 and 2025. However, Owaisi has struggled to make a similar impact in Uttar Pradesh."Owaisi has not been able to replicate his success in Bihar in Uttar Pradesh. The only time AIMIM made its presence felt was during the 2023 urban local body elections, when it won five chairperson seats and around 75 councillor seats. But these were just flashes of success, not signs of a larger political shift," Pravin Kumar said.In Bihar, Owaisi found a strong base in Seemanchal, a region with a large concentration of Muslim voters. All five seats won by AIMIM in both elections came from this region.In UP, however, AIMIM failed to win a single seat despite contesting 38 constituencies in 2017 and 95 in 2022. Its vote share in the last assembly elections was less than 1%.While Muslims account for around 19% of UP's population, their presence is spread across several regions. Owaisi is yet to establish a stronghold comparable to Seemanchal, while the SP enjoys considerable support among Muslim voters.Despite nearly a decade of contesting elections in UP, AIMIM is still looking for its first assembly seat.An alliance born out of limited choicesChandrashekhar Azad was not Owaisi's first choice for an alliance in Uttar Pradesh. The AIMIM chief had repeatedly approached Akhilesh Yadav to join hands against the BJP.When the SP showed no interest, AIMIM reached out to Mayawati's Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), hoping to bring Muslims and Dalits together. However, that attempt also failed, and Owaisi eventually joined hands with Azad.But forming an alliance is one thing and getting voters to support each other's candidates is another.While Azad enjoys support among sections of Dalit youth, his ability to mobilise Dalits across the state and transfer their votes to AIMIM candidates is yet to be tested.Similarly, Owaisi will have to convince Muslim voters to back candidates fielded by Azad's party instead of the SP. For now, both Owaisi and Azad have far more to prove in the upcoming assembly elections than Akhilesh.Samajwadi Party remains the strongest challenger to the BJPIn Uttar Pradesh, Muslim voters have largely backed parties they believe are best placed to defeat the BJP. For now, that party is the Samajwadi Party, not AIMIM.According to the CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey, around 79% of Muslim voters backed the SP-led alliance in the 2022 assembly elections. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, 92% backed the SP-Congress alliance.The alliance won 43 of UP's 80 Lok Sabha seats, with the SP alone winning 37, compared to the BJP's 33.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Akhilesh's position is also reflected in his ongoing seat-sharing negotiations with the Congress. Though the arrangement is yet to be finalised, he has made it clear that seats will be allocated based on each party's chances of winning them.While Owaisi is asking Muslims to move away from traditional political parties and build their own leadership, Akhilesh is offering them an alliance that has already demonstrated its ability to defeat the BJP.And as long as defeating the BJP remains a priority for a large section of Muslim voters in UP, convincing them to shift their support away from the SP may not be easy for Owaisi.On paper, the Owaisi-Azad alliance looks promising, with Muslims and Dalits together accounting for around 40% of UP's population. But the reality on the ground is different. Owaisi has struggled to replicate his Bihar success, while Azad is yet to establish statewide appeal. The alliance could influence closely contested seats, particularly in western UP, where Owaisi has some support.So, while the alliance may appear to be a threat to Akhilesh's PDA formula on paper, both leaders have several electoral challenges of their own to overcome.And that is perhaps why Akhilesh has little reason to be worried, at least for now.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Myanmar, China object to landmark ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide
articles.summary: A Myanmar government spokesperson said the ruling was unjust and noted that the court’s decision was not unanimous.
articles.body:
Myanmar’s government has rejected a ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) that its security forces conducted state-sponsored genocide against the country’s Rohingya minority, calling the judgement “unfair”.

Myanmar’s government spokesperson Khaing Khaing Soe told a news conference on Friday that the military government was a victim of injustice. China also criticised the verdict, a day after issuing a statement alongside the United States and Russia calling on international bodies such as the ICJ to refrain from abusing their jurisdiction.

The statements follow an ICJ ruling on Thursday that said Buddhist-majority Myanmar had committed genocide against its Muslim Rohingya minority in a crackdown in 2017.

“Our country was unjustly accused,” Soe said. “This ⁠⁠decision is not a ⁠⁠unanimous decision by everyone; it is not fair.”

China, which is allied to Myanmar’s military government, said that such rulings by the UN’s top court are “not conducive to the settlement of disputes”.

“The international community should make joint efforts in this direction to avoid complicating this issue,” Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.

The ICJ found that Myanmar’s military carried out mass executions of men and boys, committed widespread rape and sexual violence against Rohingya women, and burned or razed hundreds of villages during so-called “clearance operations”.

Of the court’s 15 judges, nine ruled in favour of declaring genocide and six ruled against. It was the first time in the ICJ’s 80-year history that its judges had determined that a state committed genocide.

One of the court’s judges is Chinese and voted in Myanmar’s favour on all but one count.

The brutal crackdown launched by Myanmar security forces nine years ago forced about 700,000 Rohingya to seek refuge in neighbouring Bangladesh. Some also fled further afield, including to Malaysia.

The ICJ’s ruling said Myanmar had an obligation to compensate the Rohingya for the violations it had committed, to be determined later, and it must also allow the “safe and dignified return” of Rohingya displaced as a ⁠⁠result of Myanmar’s “wrongful acts”.

On Friday, Malaysia said it plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya migrants in Turkiye as part of efforts to resolve the long-running refugee challenge it has faced.

Rohingya people make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, according to the United Nations.

Myanmar is in the grip of a multi-fronted civil war, including in Rakhine state where most of the country’s Rohingya lived.

articles.title: Senate foreign relations chairman warns of 'horrific trend' as Christians killed in Ethiopia
articles.summary: The State Department calls for independent investigations after at least 34 people were killed in Ethiopia's Arsi Zone, most said to be Ethiopian Orthodox Christians.
articles.body: The Republican chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee has warned of an ongoing ‘horrific trend’ of Christians being killed in Africa. Earlier this month, at least 34 people, the majority said to be Ethiopian Orthodox Christians, were killed in a village in the Arsi Zone, about 250 miles southeast of Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa. "The attacks on Christians in Ethiopia are a horrific trend," Sen. Jim Risch, R-Idaho, told Fox News Digital in a statement, adding, "The instability and violence in Ethiopia has grave consequences for Ethiopian civilians, the region and American interests." NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES Open Doors UK & Ireland told Fox News Digital there has been a string of killings in the area, with some 60 Orthodox Christians killed just two weeks before this attack in November. Open Doors is an international organization supporting persecuted Christians. A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital they are aware of "reports of killing in Arsi Zone," adding: "Reports of civilian killings in Ethiopia demand action. We call for independent investigations and accountability." The Addis Standard online news outlet reported gunmen approached St. Mary’s Church in Endeto, Robe District, and at the main entrance shouted "Surrender" before opening fire. Worshipers here are from the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. Local security guards, who are said to have fired back to protect community members, are believed to be among the dead. One resident told the Addis Standard, "If you asked me right now, I have no hope of staying here because I would choose to flee for long-term survival." The identity of the attackers has not yet been confirmed. An attack last month has been attributed locally to the Oromo Liberation Army, designated in Ethiopia as a terrorist organization. The State Department, quoting the Ethiopian government’s 2007 census, the most recent available, stated the country’s population is 63% Christian. One local source reports though that three of those who died in this latest attack were Muslim. SUPER BOWL CHAMP BEN WATSON SPEAKS OUT ON CHRISTIAN NIGERIAN PERSECUTION, DOUBLE-STANDARDS AND TRUMP'S IMPACT Ethiopia is ranked 36 on Open Doors’ World Watch List of countries where Christians are most persecuted. The organization stated "Open Doors condemns the violence against Orthodox Christians and calls on the Government of Ethiopia to take proactive measures to protect vulnerable civilians from attacks by armed groups operating in the area. Reports from the field point to horrific brutality against Orthodox Christians in parts of the Arsi zone of Oromia." The statement continued, "We urge the federal government to protect vulnerable communities, including Orthodox Christians, particularly in areas where armed groups are active. We also call on the government to hold perpetrators accountable and help all those affected rebuild their lives." ANOTHER CHRISTIAN COMMUNITY AT RISK IN AFRICA AS EXTREMISTS AND WAR TAKE THEIR TOLL Open Doors states the recent attacks in the area started in 2025, when 25 people were killed. The attacks have ramped up this year: In February, attackers stormed a church and a market in East Arsi, killing more than 20 Orthodox Christians and one Muslim guard. In March, 21 people were reportedly killed in East Arsi Zone. In May, the 101-year-old Teleta Holy Gabriel Church was destroyed and 50 killed in multiple attacks. In October, 14 people were killed in Gora Singo and in the Arsi Zone, 46 were killed in multiple attacks. This led to the U.S. Ambassador to Ethiopia Ervin J. Masinga posting, "Such horrific attacks against any group must stop." In November, at least 34 were killed in Endeto. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Senate Foreign Affairs Chairman Risch added, "It is imperative that Ethiopia find a way to manage its domestic affairs in a way that addresses longstanding grievances and promotes sustained peace." With fighting continuing in several parts of the country, especially in the border area around Eritrea, the State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "Fighting in several regions of Ethiopia is a concern. We urge all parties to protect civilians and resolve disputes through dialogue." Fox News Digital reached out to the Ethiopian government, but received no response.

articles.title: Outages in US cause worry, despite official attempts to downplay concerns
articles.summary: Experts say Trump administration is not taking the threat of AI attacks seriously, as consumers stock up on supplies.
articles.body:
Consumers in the United States have dealt with a number of technology-related outages in the last week, affecting services provided by major banks and companies such as Microsoft , Workday, and Apple.

Even the US government has experienced problems, including a national aviation ground stop and an ongoing problem affecting the internal network at the country’s premier surveillance agency .

US officials have downplayed suggestions that the incidents are related.

“Tell them to relax, everything is good, these are individual events,” US President Donald Trump told a reporter on Fox on Thursday when asked about the outages and whether the public should be preparing for emergencies.

The White House fired the US cybersecurity chief on Thursday and appointed a replacement, days after the disruptions.

US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said in media interviews on Wednesday that the outages likely stemmed from organisations using artificial intelligence (AI) to fix security flaws and carry out maintenance updates.

The tech outages come after months of public alarm over the threat posed by AI, as well as messaging by governments in the US and other countries about other events that has inadvertently added to that concern.

In the UK, Sweden, and Japan, for example, authorities have run campaigns in recent months to remind the public to store essentials at home such as torches, water, and medicine, in case they experience stronger-than-usual storms this winter due to the El Nino phenomenon. Last month, the US Department of Defense announced it was rolling out a programme to ensure all military bases could operate for 90 days without relying on the civilian power grid.

“It’s been an unusual stretch. People have had problems with several services they rely on in their daily lives, and we’re still learning what happened in some of these cases,” said Danny Atherton, a lecturer at Georgetown University and editor of the AI Incident Database, which tracks global outages and attacks reported to have involved the use of AI.

“I worry most about essential services,” Atherton said. “If a shared system goes down, can a hospital still take care of patients? … I think governments and AI providers should expect serious outages to continue.”

More and more companies are using AI to test their systems and finding vulnerabilities that could potentially be exploited by malicious actors in unexpected ways.

Last month, the FBI said cybercriminals linked to the North Korean government were able to steal $6bn in cryptocurrency from the Binance crypto exchange. The hackers reportedly used AI in several parts of the complex operation, posing as recruiters from another company to conduct video interviews with engineers, planting malicious software on their computers, and eventually gaining access to crypto wallets holding the funds.

Peter Slattery, a research scientist at MIT’s FutureTech, said the Binance heist is one example of how AI might have played a role in the series of outages in recent weeks, but may not yet have been noticed. Malicious actors could have used AI to conduct research, or create deepfakes that were convincing enough to win the trust of key employees at target companies. Software may have been updated to accommodate AI tools, or it might have recommended changes to how a company operates that turned out to be problematic.

“We are moving into an era where AI is increasingly useful, both for hacking and for a variety of other tools,” Slattery told Al Jazeera. “It’s quite likely, but not guaranteed, that things will get worse. We will have more attacks from AI on infrastructure, and there will be some significant attacks and harmful events over the next year or two.”

Slattery points out that companies are already seeking to insulate themselves from liability if a potential AI-powered attack happens. In the last few months, for instance, several major banks, including JP Morgan, Citibank, and Bank of America, have notified customers that if they use third-party tools that use AI to access their accounts, the banks will not be liable for any losses if something goes wrong.

The speed with which Trump administration officials have brushed off questions about the threat posed by recent outages has also reduced confidence among experts, like Deanne Criswell, who served as the head of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) until 2025.

“We can’t just take the first answers as the absolute answers, because sometimes these vulnerabilities can be buried deep within the system, and we have to do our due diligence to understand the cause,” Criswell told Al Jazeera.

She said that incidents like the airline ground stop last week should not be treated in the same way as natural disasters. After a hurricane, FEMA officials can fairly quickly assess the damage, and estimate how long it would take to restore critical services, whether that is days, or weeks, or even months later.

“But in a cyber or tech-related incident, I don’t know that, I’m not an expert in that, and I have to bring in those outside partners … to help us better understand the cause,” Criswell explained.

FEMA relied on the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to do that, Criswell said, but it is unclear what the impact of budget and staff cuts has been at the agency under Trump.

The agency is tasked with maintaining contact with the myriad of private companies that control everything from water to power and telecommunications in the US. More than a third of its staff were lost to cuts by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) in 2025, and in the administration’s proposed budget for 2027, CISA would face $700m in cuts.

The measures demonstrate “a dangerous underestimation of the threats facing our nation from adversaries and criminals who seek to destabilise our national security, economy, public health, and safety”, Democratic Senator Mark Warner of the state of Virginia wrote to the agency in June.

Emergency preparedness becoming more mainstream

Regardless of official messaging, or what might actually be to blame for the incidents, they are not going unnoticed by the US public, said Chris Ellis, a disaster preparedness expert and Director of Education and Strategic Outreach for The American Civil Defense Association.

More and more people in the US have sought to collect supplies such as food, water, and other essentials in recent years, especially after moments of crisis, like the outbreak of the Ukraine war, or the global pandemic. After each election, Ellis says, the losing side in the US has also tended to purchase emergency supplies. In 2024, more than 20 million Americans had enough supplies to last them 31 days or longer after a disaster, according to Ellis – a number that has grown in recent years and months.

Regardless of government efforts to calm public fears, Ellis says the proportion of people who are actively preparing for a disaster is reaching the point where the practice might be normalised, as it was in previous generations, or still is in some other countries.

“We are kind of at that stage where prepping is still seen as fringe, but not crazy,” he said.

articles.title: Hulme Hippodrome campaigners want to buy theatre after no sale at auction
articles.summary: Hulme Hippodrome was listed at auction on Thursday but failed to sell.
articles.body:
Locals who have campaigned to try to save a historical theatre from demolition say they want to buy it after it failed to sell at auction.

Hulme Hippodrome in Manchester was listed for a reserve price of £895,000, but on Thursday bidding failed to reach that mark.

The Grade II-listed building was last used for theatre in the 1960s, and has since hosted live recordings of BBC shows, bingo events, and a church congregation. It has been left empty since 2017.

Paul Baker, from the Save Hulme Hippodrome campaign group, said they had been "chasing this building for five years" because it represents "working-class culture in this city" so he was "really pleased" it was still available.

"We thought the price was too high, and so didn't think it was going to get sold," he told BBC Radio Manchester .

Baker said the group had since decided to investigate whether its members could raise the money needed to bring the theatre into community ownership.

"This gives us a fresh opportunity. We've decided we're going to come up with a community share offer," he said.

The community ownership model allows local people to own shares in properties such as pubs, former schools, and performance venues .

Baker said the building was "so important", adding: "We want Hulme Hippodrome to be represented in the cultural offer of Manchester."

He said the campaign group had "a master plan" to save the building, and that they would seek to raise about £400,000 for the purchase, or rely on an angel investor to buy it for philanthropic reasons and then lease the site.

"We aren't just sitting around lobbying, we've been actually working really hard to find out how we can realistically, reliably bring this building back into use and make it part of what can happen in the future."

A spokesperson for NovaLoca, who are auctioning the building on behalf of the current owners real estate firm HHM 20 Ltd, said new offers had been made for the old theatre but that they were "substantially below" the original asking price.

On the subject of it being owned by the community, they said: "The problem with groups owning it is often how they raise the funds, compared with companies who have the business nouse and track record with money.

"There's so much to be spent on the internals, so the group would have to crowdfund to buy it but then have enough for the renovation."

Hulme Hippodrome will next go to auction on 17 December.

articles.summary: US ambassador to India Sergio Gor on Friday described New Delhi as one of America's most trusted partners, saying the two countries' defence partnership
articles.body: US ambassador to India Sergio Gor on Friday described New Delhi as one of America's most trusted partners, saying the two countries' defence partnership will define the 21st century, during a visit aboard the US aircraft carrier USS George Washington (CVN-73) in the Indian Ocean.According to news agency ANI, Gor made the remarks while addressing personnel aboard the USS George Washington, where he described India as one of the few countries Washington "truly trust[s]" and said the partnership would define the 21st century."When America says it will show up, it shows up. And we know that when the moment calls, India, our trusted major defence partner, will also show up," Gor said.Gor said US President Donald Trump had made the relationship with India a top priority, pointing to New Delhi's access to American technology, training, military planning and engagement between senior leadership. He stressed that the partnership was not limited to defence transactions but was based on long-term strategic cooperation."When we meet with your leaders, the conversation is not transactional. It is strategic, candid, and forward-looking," Gor said, referring to the 10-year framework for the US-India Major Defence Partnership signed in October 2025.Gor also highlighted the two countries' expanding military cooperation through joint exercises, saying India conducts more military exercises with the US than with any other country.Citing engagements across different military domains, he referred to exercises such as Tarang Shakti and Yudh Abhyas, besides the recently concluded Tiger Triumph in Visakhapatnam and Malabar naval exercise off the coast of Japan.Referring to Tiger Triumph, Gor said the two sides integrated operational cyber elements for the first time, while Malabar demonstrated the growing coordination between their navies in high-end maritime warfare. He said the exercises were helping build interoperability across land, sea and air.The fifth edition of Tiger Triumph was conducted from October 31 to November 5, 2026, with a focus on humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operations. The ministry of defence said the exercise involved joint planning and exchanges on contemporary domains, including cyberspace.The USS George Washington's presence in the Indian Ocean comes after a nearly three-month deployment in the Middle East. The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier arrived in the region on August 19 to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-71) and support US naval operations under the 5th Fleet, before returning to the US Navy's 7th Fleet area of operations on November 18, according to USNI News.The carrier is homeported at Yokosuka, Japan, and is now resuming routine Indo-Pacific operations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Colombian president calls out 'false' New York Times report on US partnership against narcoterrorism
articles.summary: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella called a report from The New York Times that says he rejected a joint U.S. operation against narcoterrorism "false."
articles.body: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella said Wednesday that a New York Times report claiming he rejected a joint military operation with the U.S. to combat narcoterrorism was "false." The New York Times reported that, according to U.S. officials, de la Espriella said he lacked the votes in Congress to approve working with the Pentagon and the Trump administration, which the publication described as "a major setback for the Trump administration’s campaign against drug gangs." The agreement would have allowed U.S. forces to carry out joint airstrikes and ground operations within Colombia. The article was published under the headline "Colombia Rejects Joint Plan With U.S. to Target Drug Gangs." ‘WAVE OF FREEDOM’ SWEEPS LATIN AMERICA AS TRUMP ALLY TAKES FIGHT TO MARXIST TERROR GROUP In an X post, de la Espriella denied rejecting any proposal from the Trump administration, insisting that the two countries maintain "strong and increasingly close cooperation" with each other. "The information published by The New York Times, claiming that I rejected a plan for cooperation with the United States to conduct joint operations against narcoterrorism, is false," de la Espriella wrote. De la Espriella added that a request to allow foreign troops into Colombia would fall under the jurisdiction of the country's Congress rather than his office and that he would continue to work with the U.S. to help strengthen Colombian forces. ECUADOR'S PRESIDENT DENIES US OPERATES MILITARY BASE DESPITE REPORTS OF TROOP BUILDUP "Any decision will be made in accordance with our Constitution, national sovereignty, and the relevant legal procedures. Our alliance with the United States is stronger than ever, and we have a common enemy: NARCOTERRORISM. Stand firm for the Homeland! Long live Christ the King!" de la Espriella wrote. The New York Times also reported that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth altered the schedule of his Latin America trip in response to the lack of a deal. In response, Hegseth similarly called out the report for casting doubt on the relationship between the nations. TRUMP CLEARS HURDLE IN $15 BILLION LAWSUIT AGAINST NEW YORK TIMES "Amen, Mr. President. The fake news cannot help themselves. Totally false. Our partnership to defeat the narco-terrorists that threaten your country, and ours, is stronger than ever before. The @DeptofWar is with you all the way," Hegseth wrote on X. In a statement to Fox News Digital, The New York Times pointed to a statement the publication released on X. "Our reporting confirmed that President Abelardo De La Espriella of Colombia told U.S. officials that his nation would not allow American forces to take part in anti-cartel military operations on its soil. Our reporters reached out multiple times to Mr. De La Espriella’s press team for a response prior to publication, but they chose not to comment," the statement read. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It continued, "After our story ran, Mr. De La Espriella said on X that it was ‘false’ that his government had rejected a cooperation plan. We have updated our story to include his response and stand by the details and sourcing in this story." Fox News Digital also reached out to the White House for comment.

articles.title: Aberdeen police trialling use of AI-assisted CCTV cameras
articles.summary: The software uses key words to help officers search thousands of images.
articles.body:
Police in Aberdeen are trialling the use of AI-assisted CCTV technology to help track down suspects and missing people.

The software - known as BriefCam - allows operators to search with key words and descriptions of clothing or vehicles to narrow down available footage.

The pilot, which uses a network of 100 existing cameras in the city, runs until the middle of December and could be rolled out nationally.

The force insisted the system was safe, accurate, and would not invade people's privacy.

More stories from North East Scotland, Orkney and Shetland

Listen to news from North East Scotland on BBC Sounds

The trial period started in September and covers the city centre, Torry, Mastrick and Rosemount areas.

A consultation on the plans earlier this year received "mixed reviews".

As well as searching key prompts it can also help show the direction of travel and speed cars are travelling at.

While the cameras can deploy facial recognition technology this trial does not use it. Any future use of that technology would need to go through a similar trial process.

Ass Ch Con Tim Mairs said at this stage Police Scotland had "no intention" to switch that capability on.

He said the system it was testing was "accurate and helpful".

"What is really key about this is it is a tool that is used by very experienced and qualified CCTV operators," he added.

"It is a really good tool to support our staff, but it does not replace the staff.

"It does not look at facial images or biometrics or skin colour, but what it can do is look at clothing and it can look at sort of body shapes and rucksacks and things like that."

Mair said the tool could reduce tens of thousands of images down to 15 or 16 for further examination.

Police Scotland said in one recent case it helped trace an elderly woman by analysing nine hours of footage in an hour.

It reduced 8,000 objects down to six possible options.

Mairs said he appreciated some members of the public may have privacy concerns over the use of the cameras.

But he believed a "modern police force" should be using AI technology.

He said: " We also want to ensure that we maintain and uphold the human rights of the people that we serve, not undermine them.

"The likes of this evaluation allows us to sit back and look at all the data, then we take those considerations to the Scottish Police Authority who hold us to account in public."

The senior officer added: "We are not seeing anything that would massively concern us or even slightly concern us about impact on human rights."

articles.title: 15 dead, 150 undergoing treatment after suspected methanol poisoning from liquor in Manipur
articles.summary: IMPHAL: At least 15 people have died and around 150 patients are undergoing treatment at Shija Hospitals and Research Institute in Imphal following a
articles.body: IMPHAL: At least 15 people have died and around 150 patients are undergoing treatment at Shija Hospitals and Research Institute in Imphal following a suspected methanol poisoning incident linked to the consumption of locally made liquor at Chakpi Karong in Manipur's Chandel district.The affected people are mostly residents of Chakpi Karong and nearby areas of Chandel district, and include adults and middle-aged individuals, according to available information.Many of those brought to the hospital displayed symptoms consistent with methanol poisoning, suspected to have resulted from consuming locally made liquor contaminated with the toxic substance.The situation at Shija Hospital remains critical, with patients continuing to arrive for emergency treatment. Another bus carrying affected people was reportedly on its way to the hospital, raising concerns that the number of casualties and hospitalisations could increase further.Chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh also visited Shija Hospital to assess the situation and meet patients and medical teams.Speaking to ANI, Dr Chetan Hundongbam, Joint Managing Director of Shija Hospital, said, "Today we received news prior to the incoming patients that some poisoning had occurred in Chandel district, and on arrival of the patients, we found out that it was methanol poisoning, mainly from the Chakpi Karong area. Till now, we have received 140 patients, out of which one has expired—he was brought dead. Three are critical and undergoing hemodialysis, which is the cleansing of the kidneys."Pointing to the pressure on the hospital's capacity, Dr Hundongbam added, "Right now, the beds which we have prepared are overwhelmed, and we have requested the State Health Department, RIMS, as well as GENIMS to help us in treating the patients. We will be referring patients to the other centres, and we will take the more critical patients who require any life support or hemodialysis treatment here. The honourable CM has come and assured all patients that whatever can be done from the state health department will be done."Meanwhile, Sumil Langhu from the Chandel District Headquarters told ANI that the outbreak had been unfolding over the past two to three days."In the last two to three days, we came across this outbreak. From the source that I received, it is basically from consuming liquor. Where the liquor comes from, I am not able to give surety, but as per the report we received, it is because of this liquor that they consumed," Langhu said.Sharing details of the toll and treatment at different facilities, he added, "So far, 15 people have died as of this evening, as far as my knowledge is concerned. Right now at Shija, we have 150 patients who have come for tests, and many more patients are also at Babina undergoing the same treatment. This is a very unfortunate incident, but with the support that we received today from our honourable CM, we are very happy with the financial assistance that he has assured us."(With inputs from ANI)Stay updated with the latest Imphal news. articles.title: Jensen Huang told one employee his mother should have aborted him; yelled at another that he would remove the top of their head and urinate on their brain: NYT investigation
articles.summary: Jensen Huang, the billionaire co-founder of Nvidia who built the company into one of the world's most valuable technology giants, allegedly ran a
articles.body: Jensen Huang, the billionaire co-founder of Nvidia who built the company into one of the world's most valuable technology giants, allegedly ran a workplace culture in which employees were routinely humiliated, insulted and threatened, according to a new investigation by NYT detailing decades of his management practices. Huang, who resigned as Nvidia's chief executive on November 12 following revelations about multiple extramarital relationships including with a suspected Chinese spy, allegedly used public humiliation as a management tool, because he believed that his employees became so rich that he could no more motivate them with money. And so he used to deliberately pile on them.A New York Times investigation, published on November 20 and based on interviews with more than a dozen current and former employees, as well as hundreds of pages of court records and other documents, has detailed allegations about Huang's behaviour dating back more than two decades. According to the investigation, Huang's management style involved savage personal insults, threats of physical violence and humiliating employees in front of their colleagues. Some employees described the workplace as a culture of fear, even as others remained fiercely loyal to the billionaire.'I will rip your heart out and stomp on it'The allegations about Huang's management style date back to 2004, when Michael Winston joined Nvidia as its senior vice president of human resources.Winston, who had previously worked at Merrill Lynch and Motorola, was reportedly shocked by the condition of Nvidia's HR department. Two senior HR officials had recently resigned, while several others were considering leaving.In October 2004, Huang allegedly unleashed a series of violent threats during a two-day company retreat attended by approximately 50 employees.According to notes Winston made at the time, Huang told employees: "You have to do this, or I will rip your fucking heart out and stomp on it."Winston later described the incident as an extended episode of public humiliation and intimidation."I watched them helpless, as they were publicly humiliated, indeed tormented, for extended periods of time, by this lunatic!" he wrote in his notes.Winston said several employees approached him afterwards, describing themselves as terrified and asking him to intervene.He did. He raised concerns with senior executives, one of whom reportedly acknowledged that Huang's behaviour was typical but could expose the company to legal liability. Another advised him to toughen up.When Winston confronted Huang, Huang reportedly dismissed the concerns and defended public humiliation as a rite of passage for employees. Winston claimed that Huang told him he subjected new recruits to such treatment during their first six months to test whether they could withstand it.According to Winston's notes, Huang also said the practice had entertainment value.HR executive fired after confronting billionaire CEOThe dispute between Winston and Huang escalated in November 2004. Winston was called into a meeting with Huang and another executive and was then fired. Huang reportedly told him that he was not a good fit for the company. The former HR chief alleged that Huang threatened to ensure he would never find another job in Silicon Valley if he sued Nvidia.In notes written after his dismissal, Winston rejected the company's explanation that he had simply been an unsuitable employee.He argued that the real reason for his termination was his objection to Huang's behaviour. Winston filed a formal complaint with California's Department of Fair Employment and Housing, alleging that he had been dismissed for opposing the treatment of employees, including conduct he characterized as sexual harassment. He also prepared a lawsuit against Nvidia and Huang. But before the complaint was formally filed, the two sides reached a confidential settlement. Nvidia paid Winston more than $1 million, according to the investigation. Neither side admitted liability or wrongdoing as part of the settlement. Winston later returned to the banking industry and became a whistleblower against Countrywide Financial Corporation over its conduct before the 2008 financial crisis. He died earlier in 2026.The NYT investigation cited more such accounts from ex-employees. One employee was allegedly told by Huang that their mother should have aborted them. Another was reportedly threatened with having both arms ripped off and being beaten to death with them.Huang also allegedly told an employee that he would remove the top of their head and urinate on their brain.Huang's aggressive management style influenced his daughter Madison Huang, who continues to work at the company. Madison reportedly functioned as her father's de facto chief of staff and was accused by six current and former employees of frequently shouting at colleagues, including executives who were senior to her.In one incident during a call with Nvidia's marketing team last year, she allegedly repeatedly berated a vice president.The executive eventually left the meeting, saying: "I'm having an anxiety attack. I'm going to drop off. I'm sorry."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Denmark says it thwarted Russian plot to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary: Danish police averted an attempt by Russian intelligence services to assassinate a US-Ukrainian rapper in September ahead of a planned performance, police and security officials said on Friday.
articles.body: Danish police averted an attempt by Russian intelligence services to assassinate a US-Ukrainian rapper in September ahead of a planned performance, police and security officials said on Friday. Soon after the announcement, Denmark said it was expelling Russia’s defense attache in the country in protest, with Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen calling the alleged plot an unacceptable transgression. “We don’t want to break off diplomatic relations with Russia in this particular situation that Denmark and Europe are in… But on the other hand, we want to send a very, very strong signal,” Rasmussen said. The Russian embassy in Copenhagen said the accusations were not backed with proof. “In keeping with what has become a poor tradition, the Danish side has not bothered to present any evidence whatsoever of Russia’s involvement in this mysterious crime, nor have they submitted a request for legal assistance,” the embassy said in an emailed statement. Moscow has regularly denied accusations of stepping up hybrid attacks – incidents of aggression that fall short ​of acts of war – in the region following its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Prosecutors say suspects had loaded pistols and knives Police thwarted the attempt when they arrested three men with links to the Danish criminal underworld shortly before the rapper Kyivstoner was due to give a concert north of Copenhagen on September 25, police and security officials told a press conference. “It is our clear assessment that the assassination attempt was planned by the Russian intelligence services,” Rasmus Kieffer-Kristensen, head of Denmark’s national security and intelligence service, PET, said. The police and security services made their announcements as two Danish men appeared in court near Copenhagen on Friday, charged under Section 108 of Denmark’s Criminal Code, which covers assisting a foreign intelligence service, as well as attempted murder, court documents showed. Both men denied wrongdoing, broadcaster DR reported. In the court documents, prosecutors said the men were driving towards the venue with two loaded pistols and two knives when police arrested them at around 9.55 p.m. local time, five minutes before the concert was due to begin. One of the suspects had bought a ticket to the concert, according to the charges. The concert was cancelled. “A Russian assassination attempt is not something we’ve seen in Denmark before, and that gives me an impression of an increasingly aggressive and risk-taking Russia,” Kieffer-Kristensen told the press conference. “We believe that the case is important for understanding the threat that Denmark faces from Russia.” PET said in September Russia was recruiting Danish citizens to help plan sabotage against Danish defense firms with ties to Ukraine.
