articles.title: 'Look at India', 'country of second chances': 10 key takeaways from Trump's first presser since midterm loss
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday defended his administration's policies following the Republican Party's midterm losses, while signalling an openness
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Friday defended his administration's policies following the Republican Party's midterm losses, while signalling an openness to working with Democrats on immigration and other domestic issues. At his first major White House news conference since the election setback, Trump referenced India's economic growth, highlighted the Quad's commercial potential, backed former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return to the chipmaker by describing the US as a "country of second chances", and reiterated that he wanted a deal with Iran but would not accept terms he considered inadequate.Trump also threatened to use his veto powers to push the incoming Democratic House majority into negotiations, defended his approach to China and advanced chip exports, and outlined plans to restrict US companies from building data centres overseas. The nearly 90-minute briefing also featured remarks from Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.Here are the 10 key takeaways from the presser:Quad, India feature in Trump's remarksTrump highlighted the economic and strategic potential of the Quad, comprising the US, India, Japan and Australia, pointing to cooperation on economic security, supply chains and maritime security.He praised the grouping's economic strength, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said its members were "four very powerful economies" that could work together to create jobs and markets for American products.The Quad is also planning its inaugural Business Leaders' Forum in early 2027, with India set to host the first edition in Mumbai.Trump separately praised India's economic performance, citing its growth rate and interest-rate environment. "Look at India, they have low interest rates, and they have a seven per cent growth rate," he said, suggesting the US could achieve much higher growth with lower interest rates. Trump says Iran wants a deal, but not one acceptable to himTrump said Iran was interested in reaching an agreement with the US but was unwilling to accept terms that Washington would consider satisfactory. He linked the price of gasoline in the US to the outcome of negotiations with Tehran."They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me," Trump said."We want to make a real deal, not a fake deal that they've been doing for 51 years," he added, accusing Iran of "b*****i**ng people for 51 years".Trump also reiterated that he would make the decision to launch military action against Iran again if given another opportunity, arguing that the US could not allow Tehran to acquire nuclear weapons.He said: "The answer is absolutely yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon."Trump also backed Vice President JD Vance's assessment that the Iran war had contributed to Republican losses in the midterm elections, calling his statement "a very accurate" one. However, he maintained that the military action was necessary.The trilateral with Xi and PutinTrump described his first trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping as a historic step towards reducing nuclear risks, claiming the three countries had agreed to work together to prevent nuclear conflict.He said that Beijing had agreed to trilateral discussions on reducing nuclear risks, while the three leaders had declared that nuclear conflict must never be allowed."The United States, Russia, and China formally agreed that nuclear conflict must never be allowed to happen," Trump said, describing the summit as a "first of its kind trilateral peace declaration".Trump acknowledged that complete denuclearisation would be difficult, saying he viewed nuclear weapons more as a deterrent. He also reiterated that the US would not allow Iran to acquire a nuclear weapon.Read more: 'Discussed responsibility as world's 3 largest nuclear powers' - Trump on first-ever trilateral with Xi, PutinSupport for Jensen HuangTrump voiced support for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, saying he would like to see him return to the company despite its board accepting his resignation and indicating it did not intend to reinstate him."He made some bad decisions, but he is a brilliant person," Trump said, crediting Huang with helping the US maintain its lead in the artificial intelligence chip industry."I would love to see him back. You know, we're a country of second chances, and I'd love to be able to see him. That's a very important company to us, and he put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies," he said.Trump also claimed he had discussed Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who he said had described the former Nvidia chief as brilliant. "And I think the company, if they were smart, they'd take that brilliant man, accept an apology, and let him go back to work," Trump added.He compared his defence of Huang with his earlier support for Elon Musk, saying the US needed to protect talented people. Trump recalled how he had defended Musk during his first term, saying: “I came to Elon’s defence in my first term very strongly. I’m not sure Elon would be with us if I didn’t. I said, ‘We have to protect our brilliant people.’ Because no country has too many of them.”He also praised Musk's current work, particularly Starlink, saying: “Elon is doing some amazing things right now with everything he’s doing. Starlink. I mean, what he’s done is pretty amazing.”Trump also defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick amid scrutiny over his approach to Nvidia and advanced chip exports to China. Republican Senator Tom Cotton had accused Lutnick of ignoring warnings about AI chips being smuggled into China."I have not lost confidence," Trump said of Lutnick. "He has a natural business instinct. I think he's doing a very good job."Acknowledging differences between Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent over China policy, Trump described the commerce secretary as "a different kind of guy" and a "natural businessman".'Only older chips should be sold to China'Trump reiterated that the US should restrict sales of its most advanced computer chips to China, while leaving the door open to exports of older-generation processors."We want only older chips, and we don't mind if none go, but only older," he said.He argued that China would develop its own chips if American companies were prevented from selling there."You have to understand China makes chips too, and if we're not going to sell them, they'll make them themselves," Trump said.The comments come as Washington tightens restrictions aimed at preventing China from accessing advanced AI chips made by companies such as Nvidia. Trump also said the US was discussing a "very comprehensive deal" with China, without giving further details.Rare praise for Democrat leadersTrump struck a more conciliatory note towards Democrats when discussing his recent conversation with Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, saying he believed they could work together on border security. Hinojosa, a Democrat, had called him, Trump said, describing the conversation as “very productive”.“She was really nice. It was a very productive call. And she wants to have a strong border. And we'll be able, I think, we'll be able to work something out,” he said.Trump also avoided criticising New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, with whom he has maintained an unexpectedly cordial relationship. While taking aim at Democratic-led cities over their cleanliness, infrastructure and crime, Trump said he did not want to target New York because he got along well with its mayor.“I don’t want to mention New York, because I actually get along very well with Mayor Mamdani, but I could if I wanted to. But I won’t do that because I like relationships,” Trump said.The remarks came as Trump compared US cities with Shenzhen, praising Chinese President Xi Jinping for keeping the city “clean” and “immaculate”. He criticised conditions in several American cities, particularly those run by Democrats, and singled out Chicago and Los Angeles.Trump threatens to use veto power to push Democrats into dealsTrump said he planned to use his presidential veto power to pressure the incoming Democratic House majority into negotiating with his administration.He described the power to pardon and the power to veto as two of the presidency's major powers, saying he would reject legislation until Democrats agreed to his demands."So, they're going to send things my way, and I'm going to veto them. And then they're going to send more things, and I'm going to veto them," he said.He suggested that after repeated vetoes, Democrats would be more willing to negotiate."But I think after a month or so, they're going to send things, and I'm going to say, I'm going to veto unless you want to do this and this and this," Trump added.Despite the threat, he praised Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to become the next House speaker, calling him "smart" and "streetwise"."If they want to get things done, I want to get things done too," Trump said. He also expressed willingness to work with Democrats on healthcare, saying there was a "real possibility" of reaching an agreement.Trump threatens 'tremendous tax' on data centres built overseasTrump said US companies would face a "tremendous tax" if they built data centres in other countries, arguing that the infrastructure was important to maintaining America's lead in artificial intelligence."We're not allowing data centers to go into other countries," he said.Trump did not provide details of how the proposed tax would work and acknowledged that he had not yet informed officials about the plan.He also urged local communities to welcome data centre projects and negotiate benefits from developers rather than oppose construction. He argued that companies could build their own electricity infrastructure, potentially reducing power costs for communities.Read more: 'China will take all of them' - Trump says won't let US firms build data centres abroad Trade dealsTrump highlighted trade agreements reached with Thailand and the Philippines during his recent Asia trip, saying his administration expected to secure more agreements with other countries.He said around 10 additional trade deals could be reached, pointing to the administration's efforts to expand access for American products and strengthen commercial ties.Trump also discussed trade negotiations with other countries, including Canada and Mexico, indicating that further work was needed to reach agreements. He said the US would seek terms that he believed were favourable to American businesses and workers.Read more: Two deals done, 10 more in pipeline - Trump's trade promise after Asia trip Addressing cyber chief's removal, recent tech-related outagesTrump confirmed that he had removed White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross because he did not believe the official was performing well enough."I didn't think that person was good enough," he said.The president also discussed the overhaul of the country's ageing air traffic control system, saying he had instructed Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to avoid spending money on upgrades that would eventually be replaced."I said, Sean, let's not spend money to patch up all over the place, 'cause when we get the new system, everything's gonna be torn out," Trump said.Calling the existing system "ancient", Trump said he wanted one primary contractor to coordinate its modernisation rather than multiple companies working independently. The comments came as lawmakers questioned the use of $12.5 billion already approved for the overhaul and the administration's request for another $50 billion.Trump also blamed technology upgrades for a series of recent disruptions across the US, saying such changes could sometimes cause problems. He described the incidents as "separate events"."We have thousands of companies that are upgrading right now, and when they upgrade, bad things happen," he said.The disruptions included a nationwide ground stop following an FAA network failure, a Microsoft outage affecting Outlook and Teams, and banking problems reported by customers of several major lenders.Vance, Rubio defend administration's positions; Miller also takes podiumUS VP Vance reiterated that preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon was essential, after his earlier comments linking the war to Republican midterm losses."The goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we need to be doing. It's the biggest state sponsor of terrorism," he said.He added that the president was responsible for decisions on military action and that his role was to support him. "My goal is and my job is to support the president of the United States," Vance said.Rubio, meanwhile, defended Trump's trilateral engagement with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, saying it was important for leaders of the three countries to maintain regular communication."The idea that these three leaders should not engage on a regular basis is not just absurd; it's dangerous," he said, pointing to their countries' nuclear arsenals and the importance of diplomatic engagement.Towards the end of the briefing, Trump invited his new chief of staff Stephen Miller to the podium, introducing him as "the most powerful man in the world". Miller listed what he described as the administration's achievements and said the next two years would be "the greatest two years in American history".Trump then joked that Miller had performed better than Vance and Rubio and asked whether he wanted to run for president.You use AI every day. articles.title: U.K. and EU strike deals on trade and travel, pledging to rebuild ties after Brexit
articles.summary: BRUSSELS — Britain and the European Union agreed Friday to remove barriers to trade and expand travel opportunities for young people as they pledged to rebuild their strained ties with an “ambitious and dynamic” relationship.
articles.body: BRUSSELS — Britain and the European Union agreed Friday to remove barriers to trade and expand travel opportunities for young people as they pledged to rebuild their strained ties with an “ambitious and dynamic” relationship. But they left big decisions about softening or reversing Brexit for another day. In a joint statement after a summit in Brussels, the U.K. and EU confirmed agreements that will scrap border checks on plant and animal products, cut carbon taxes on some exports by linking their emissions trading schemes and let 100,000 young adults from each side live and work in the other’s countries for up to three years. Other areas remain a work in progress, with the two sides giving themselves six months to reach an agreement on the level of university fees for EU students in the U.K. and vice versa. Friday’s summit was part of efforts to forge a closer relationship, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU and six years after the divorce became final. Supporters of Brexit argued that leaving the EU’s vast free-trade area and web of rules would let Britain take back control of its borders, laws and economy, and strike new trade deals around the world. Critics say Brexit has left Britain weaker and more isolated, and new deals with countries including Australia and Japan have not made up for the economic hit from erecting barriers between Britain and its closest and biggest economic partners. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the deal is “a turning point” in EU-U.K. relations, and U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham called it a “historic moment.” “This is a good day for Britain, and this is a good day for Europe,” he said. This was only the second EU-U.K. summit since Britain became the first country to leave the world’s biggest trading bloc. Months — likely years — of negotiations lie ahead on everything from electricity markets to manufacturing rules. Burnham said the summit was a step toward undoing a decade of damage caused by the divorce. He said the two sides are “rebuilding the bridges that were broken all of those years ago” and “building a much more constructive relationship with our nearest neighbors and our largest market.” Burnham has said all options should be on the table for future relations, including rejoining the now 27-nation bloc. But he’s stressed that reversing Brexit is just one possible outcome, and far from imminent. It would need the backing not just of British voters, but the unanimous support of a mistrustful EU. Still, he has broken a long political code of silence on the option of rejoining. “We remain open to have the closest possible relationship,” European Council President António Costa said. But he also recalled the obligations of EU membership, including single-market principles on the free movement of goods, services, people and capital. Burnham says closer ties will ease the cost of living Burnham pitched the package of agreements approved Friday as a way of “cutting costs, keeping prices down in the supermarkets and creating opportunities for young people.” He said the deals could bring in 17 billion pounds ($22 billion) a year and add 0.5% to Britain’s economic output. British retailers welcomed the deal to remove checks on food and agricultural products, which will make it cheaper and easier for U.K. businesses to export to Europe. “Getting our spaghetti bolognese from Lincolnshire onto a shelf in Dublin takes hundreds of extra miles, mountains of paperwork, a vet’s signature and even the Latin name of a cow,” said Alex Freudmann, managing director of food at Marks and Spencer. Freudmann said Friday’s announcement “is a major step forward.” But nothing in U.K.-EU relations is ever quick or simple. EU negotiators want European students to pay domestic fees if they study in Britain rather than the higher fees for foreign students, something the U.K. has resisted. An EU official said negotiations had not been easy but they sensed good will to resolve the issue. The official was designated to brief reporters about the summit but only on condition that they not be named. Talks are also continuing on Britain’s desire to be included in the bloc’s “made in Europe” rules, which favor European manufacturers for public projects over rivals from China or elsewhere. Critics say the deals are a betrayal of Brexit To get the deals, the U.K. must accept some EU rules and standards that it has no role in setting. Supporters of Brexit say that undermines Britain’s independence. Nigel Farage, leader of the euroskeptic, anti-immigration party Reform UK, told reporters in Brussels that Burnham had taken “the first step, incrementally, to take us back into membership of the European Union.” The war in Ukraine, and the U.K.’s military strength, are drawing the two sides back together, and the summit produced pledges of stronger cooperation on security and defense, as well as efforts to restrict irregular migration. Nevertheless, feelings remain raw, and EU officials have been reluctant to encourage talk of the U.K. rejoining. They are weary from the shifting demands of seven British prime ministers over the last decade and want clarity about the country’s intentions. Von der Leyen said that a lot has changed in their relations since the Brexit vote, including the pandemic and Russia’s war on Ukraine. She said that the EU is “totally open to do the necessary brainstorming for the wider picture, the bigger picture” of what ties could look like in the future. Burnham said he wanted the two sides to do that brainstorming before their next summit, probably a year from now. For now, Burnham remains bound by the pledge made by Keir Starmer, his predecessor as Labour Party leader and prime minister, not to rejoin the bloc’s tariff-free customs union or frictionless single market, or to restore free movement for EU nationals to the U.K. He acknowledged Friday’s agreements are “the limit of what we can achieve” before a national election. “Incremental steps … only take us so far,” he said.

articles.title: Russia pummels Ukraine, missile hits Poland, after Putin threat
articles.summary: Russia pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least seven people were killed in the capital, while neighbouring Poland accused Mosc...
articles.body:
Russia pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least seven people were killed in the capital, while neighbouring Poland accused Moscow of "provocation" after two Russian missiles likely landed in the southeast corner of the NATO country.

President Vladimir Putin had vowed a "painful" response to Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with US counterpart Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping on Thursday.

Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky called the night-time strikes one of Moscow's largest of the nearly five-year war, denouncing what he called Russian "terror".

Zelensky, who met allies in Berlin Thursday, said Putin's attempts to "redraw the world" with Xi and Trump had been a "failure".

In China, Putin said he "shared responsibility" for global peace with Xi and Trump and issued a "declaration toward peace" that made no mention of Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

AFP journalists saw people hunkered down in Kyiv's metro stations, which double as overnight air-raid shelters, sleeping on yoga mats, camping chairs and in pop-up tents.

Kateryna Liubychenko, 32, took her toddler down to try to get some sleep through the bombardment.

"It's painful to have to stop our child from living," she told AFP.

Two people were killed in Lviv in western Ukraine, power was knocked out in swathes of the country and in Kyiv, three vital transport bridges were hit, officials said.

The attacks forced one thermal power plant to halt electricity generation, energy company DTEK said, without providing more details.

Explosions rang out through the night as Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired.

Three bridges that cross the Dnipro river were hit, said Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko.

France requested a UN Security Council meeting over the strikes, saying "Russia will have to answer for its actions".

Later on Friday, Russia carried out a double-tap strike on the central city of Kryvyi Rig, killing a 7-year-old, as well as a 20-year-old rescuer, local authorities said.

In neighbouring Poland, authorities said one missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec, with another missile and a jet-powered drone suspected to have hit two other locations.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident was deliberate.

"The provocation may have been linked with the fact that there are (military) exercises taking place on the territory of Poland," said Tusk.

Thousands of European troops are taking part in exercises in southeastern Poland, training to help secure Ukraine in the event of a peace deal.

"Nobody can say that this was an innocent coincidence," Tusk said, adding he had informed NATO "straight away".

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, who is scheduled to visit Warsaw on Saturday, called the incident "clearly dangerous".

Russia, which has refused a ceasefire, has increased its strikes as temperatures dip in Ukraine, with many fearing this winter could be the worst of the war yet.

Ukraine's state energy operator reported "significant damage" to the country's energy infrastructure that had "seriously impacted the operation of the power grid".

The Black Sea port city of Odesa was in a "critical" situation with a "widespread power outage", it said -- adding blackouts were also recorded in Kyiv and 10 other regions.

Russia's military on Friday confirmed it had launched a "massive" attack with missiles and drones, saying they targeted military-industrial sites and transport infrastructure in several regions, including bridges in Kyiv.

The United Nations has reported rising civilian casualties this year as Russia intensifies its long-range strikes.

UNICEF on Friday said at least 114 children had been killed and 1,030 wounded in the first 10 months of 2026 -- "a higher number of verified child casualties than in any of the past three years".

"That is an average of more than three children killed or injured every single day," the organisation said, warning of an "alarming escalation in violence affecting children in Ukraine".

US-led talks on ending the fighting have so far shown little signs of progress, with Moscow having stuck to its hardline demands.

Putin has said a deal to end the war must be part of a wider agreement on European security.

Speaking in China on Thursday, he said any form of Ukraine-Europe military cooperation as part of that deal would be a "problem".

articles.body: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro was taken to hospital on Friday after suffering "severe abdominal pain".My father has just been taken to the hospital again after experiencing severe abdominal pain. It was obvious that this moment would come, with an active man kept imprisoned, without having stolen a single cent from public coffers, under the pretext of a “coup plot,” and having undergone more than 9 surgeries after being stabbed by a former PSOL activist, an arm of the PT, and with his health deteriorating every day in prison due to his lack of mobility and the psychological torture he suffers daily," said his son Carlos Bolsonaro in a post on X"The goal is still to kill Jair Bolsonaro. I have no words or feelings to describe this man!" he added.Initially saying that he couldn't be by his father's side, Carlos, later said that, "Since there are no family members at the hospital, I was asked to stay with him until further notice, and the request was approved. On my way there, and I’ll keep everyone updated! See you!"Carlos Bolsonaro, 43, is the second son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro and a politician who has served as a city councillor in Rio de Janeiro. A prominent supporter of his father's political movement, he has been involved in shaping the Bolsonaro family's social media strategy and political messaging. He is the brother of Flavio Bolsonaro, who contested the 2026 presidential election against Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.Meanwhile, the 71-year-old has a history of hospitalisations and surgeries following a stabbing in the abdomen during a campaign event in 2018. He has since undergone several procedures related to complications from the attack.Bolsonaro, who governed Brazil from 2019 to 2022, was sentenced to 27 years in prison last year for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 presidential election to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. He is currently serving his sentence under house arrest on medical grounds.The hospitalisation comes weeks after another setback for the Bolsonaro family in Brazil's presidential election. Jair Bolsonaro's eldest son, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, lost the October 25 runoff to incumbent Lula, who secured a fourth presidential term.Flavio subsequently left Brazil with his family and arrived in the United States after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador. articles.title: Judge rejects Alex Murdaugh's push to toss murder indictment over blood and ammo claims
articles.summary: A judge refused to dismiss murder charges against Alex Murdaugh, rejecting defense claims that SLED investigator David Owen misled the grand jury on blood spatter.
articles.body: The judge overseeing Alex Murdaugh’s double murder retrial has refused to dismiss the charges against him, dealing another legal blow to the disgraced former attorney ahead of his April court date. Attorneys for Murdaugh argued on Friday, Nov. 13, during a pre-trial hearing that South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) investigator David Owen gave misleading testimony regarding blood-spatter evidence and shotgun ammunition, saying it undermined the integrity of the grand jury proceedings. In her ruling on Friday afternoon, South Carolina Circuit Court Judge Debra R. McCaslin said that while there were major errors in the state's presentation of evidence to grand jurors, other evidence overwhelmingly supported the indictment. "Even if the challenged testimony concerning the blood spatter on the T-shirt and shotgun ammunition were excluded from consideration by the grand jury, the remaining unchallenged evidence overwhelmingly established probable cause," McCaslin wrote. ALEX MURDAUGH MAKES 'EXPLOSIVE' BID TO BLOW UP MURDER CASE HINGING ON DNA, DIRTY MONEY AND LIES: EXPERT While McCaslin refused to dismiss the murder indictment, she criticized the state's lead investigator on the case. "The Court does not take lightly Special Agent Owen’s failure to recognize and account for a laboratory report addressed directly to him prior to presenting testimony in this case," she wrote. "Oversights of this nature undermine public confidence in the integrity of the criminal justice system." McCaslin also acknowledged that evidence regarding ammunition presented to the grand jury wasn't accurate, but says there's no evidence that it was intentional. ALEX MURDAUGH LAWYERS ALLEGE ‘FABRICATED’ EVIDENCE WAS USED TO SECURE MURDER INDICTMENTS READ THE ORDER HERE: "Even accepting that the challenged testimony was inaccurate, the record presented does not establish intentional fabrication or prosecutorial misconduct," she said. The judge said Murdaugh's defense can challenge the disputed evidence at trial in April. "Any inconsistencies in prior investigative statements or forensic conclusions are matters properly addressed through cross-examination and impeachment at the upcoming trial, rather than through the pretrial dismissal of facially valid indictments," McCaslin wrote. The South Carolina Attorney General’s Office said after McCaslin's ruling: "We continue to prepare for the retrial in April." Murdaugh's defense attorneys argued that Owen misled the grand jury about alleged blood-spatter evidence found on the shirt Murdaugh was wearing on June 7, 2021, when his wife, Maggie, and son, Paul, were murdered at the family's Moselle property in Colleton County. Owen claimed that blood spatter found on Murdaugh's shirt linked him to the killings, despite earlier testing that failed to detect human blood in samples taken from the garment. At Murdaugh's first murder trial, Owen said he had no intention of misleading the grand jury and stated that he did not see the final SLED lab report until after the indictment had been issued. ALEX MURDAUGH FACES STATE PUSHBACK ON MAGGIE DNA TESTING AND PRISON LAPTOP REQUEST Prosecutors reiterated during the Nov. 13 hearing that the negative test results regarding the blood didn't necessarily invalidate the blood-spatter findings, and pointed to additional testing done by the state's expert which suggested earlier chemical treatment could have produced false negatives. SEND US A TIP Prosecutors said the expert continued to stand behind his conclusions and that Owen's testimony before the grand jury accurately captured investigators' understanding of the evidence at that point in time. ALEX MURDAUGH DEFENSE SAYS MURDER WEAPON MAY BE TIED TO SEPARATE KILLING AS JUDGE SEEKS ANSWERS Owen also told grand jurors that shotguns found on the Murdaugh property were loaded with the same combination of ammunition used to kill Paul, a claim the defense argues was false. Murdaugh's attorneys maintained that none of the recovered shotguns contained the exact combination of shells found at the murder scene. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST Prosecutors acknowledged that Owen's description of the ammunition to the grand jury may have been imprecise but argued that he had not intentionally misled jurors. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL "This was not overtly false. This was what the agent understood at the time," lead prosecutor Creighton Waters said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Murdaugh was convicted of both murders in 2023, but the South Carolina Supreme Court later overturned the convictions after finding that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced the jury . His retrial is scheduled to begin April 5, 2027.

articles.title: Two Salvadoran soldiers killed in Haiti while handling explosives
articles.summary: Two others were injured in the explosion, marking the first deaths among troops deployed to Haiti since late October.
articles.body:
Two Salvadoran soldiers have been killed in Haiti while handling explosive material, El Salvador’s army said, marking the first deaths among the roughly 2,500 troops who have been deployed to the country since late October.

Two others were injured in the explosion at one of the camps and are receiving medical care, the army said in a post on X on Friday. It did not reveal the identities of the soldiers.

The deaths come just over a month after El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele sent troops into Haiti, announcing a rescue mission to find four aviation technicians who went missing on October 18 after an attack on their vehicle near the capital, Port-au-Prince.

They were working with the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) at the time.

The rescue mission has since broadened into an offensive against Haiti’s gangs, with Salvadoran soldiers working alongside Haitian and international forces.

Salvadoran officials have said they plan to leave once the four missing technicians are found.

Wilson Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, told The Associated Press news agency earlier this month that the men were dead, although he provided no evidence. El Salvador’s government maintains they are alive.

The Haitian government has suggested it wants the deployment to be extended, and some Haitians took to the streets in Haiti and elsewhere earlier this week in large rallies to express support for the troops and Bukele.

The terms of the bilateral agreement between Haiti and El Salvador have not been revealed publicly, but according to the UN, most Salvadoran soldiers are operating outside the GSF and do not fall under the UN’s reporting mechanism for that mission.

Bukele has been promoting the intervention on social media, posting videos of strikes on homes belonging to gang leaders, and Haitian officials announced earlier this week that they retook control of the national football stadium.

Analysts, however, have questioned how much the Salvadoran deployment has contributed to recent gains and whether those gains would last.

They have also raised concerns about the risk to civilians, citing a lack of transparency around the rules of engagement and how Salvadoran troops are monitored.

On Thursday, Bukele officially launched his bid for a third presidential term . The elections are scheduled for February.

articles.title: Brazil’s former president Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized again, son says
articles.summary: Brazil’s former president Jair Bolsonaro is back in the hospital for abdominal pain, according to his son Carlos Bolsonaro.
articles.body: Brazil’s former president Jair Bolsonaro is back in the hospital for abdominal pain, according to his son Carlos Bolsonaro. Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized repeatedly over the years for abdominal issues, after he was stabbed in the stomach on the campaign trail in 2018. An ally of US President Donald Trump, he is currently under house arrest on medical grounds. Last year, he was given a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Carlos Bolsonaro said on Friday that his father was taken to the hospital again after experiencing “severe abdominal pain.” “It was obvious that this moment would come, with an active man kept imprisoned, without having stolen a single cent from public coffers, under the pretext of a ‘coup plot,’” he posted to X. Carlos Bolsonaro said his father has undergone more than nine surgeries after the 2018 stabbing and that his health had been deteriorating “every day” in captivity, citing his “lack of mobility and the psychological torture he suffers daily.” He went on to say that he is the only one of Bolsonaro’s sons that the presiding judge has allowed to visit him, twice a week for two hours. Jair Bolsonaro’s latest hospitalization comes almost a month after one of his other sons, Flavio Bolsonaro, arrived in the US after fleeing Brazil following his defeat in the 2026 presidential election, in which he lost to leftist president Lula. Flavio Bolsonaro vowed to lead his country’s opposition from the US and said he left his country to avoid imprisonment and censorship. This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.summary: SAN SALVADOR, El Salvador — Two Salvadoran soldiers were killed while working with explosives in Haiti, El Salvador’s military said on Friday, marking the first officially reported deaths under the large-scale deployment that began a month ago.
articles.body: SAN SALVADOR, El Salvador — Two Salvadoran soldiers were killed while working with explosives in Haiti, El Salvador’s military said on Friday, marking the first officially reported deaths under the large-scale deployment that began a month ago. Two more were injured, the military said, without detailing where the blast took place or what type of explosives they were working with. A Salvadoran government spokesperson said they were not immediately able to share more information. Bukele has said the operation aims to recover the missing personnel. The leader of a gang that operates in the area where they went missing has suggested in successive video messages that the four Salvadorans were killed but denied responsibility. Bukele has published several dramatic videos of strikes on gang leaders’ residences around Haiti‘s capital Port-au-Prince, and thousands of Haitians have marched in support of his intervention. However, analysts warn that without a long-term plan to secure territory, attacks could backfire on civilians. Haiti‘s government, through a task force supported by a private military contractor run by Blackwater founder Erik Prince, has since March 2025 run anti-gang operations using explosive-packed drones. This has fueled criticism from human rights groups citing civilians’ exposure to blasts in densely populated areas. The UN estimates at least 87 civilians, including 21 children, have since been killed in air operations, which now include both drone strikes and gunfire from helicopters. In August last year, two Haitian police officers were killed and two more seriously injured when an explosive drone accidentally detonated at a base near the capital. Authorities said local residents had brought the faulty drone in to police after its operator lost contact with the device due to poor weather, but it exploded soon after. Early this month, US authorities said three Salvadoran soldiers were injured and one airlifted out of Haiti for treatment. Washington has endorsed Bukele’s mission, which is operating under a bilateral agreement with Haiti‘s government.
